chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Abdullah ibn Ali al-Sarrad, who said:

Abu Kahmas asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'Should a man pray his optional prayers in one place or distribute them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he should distribute them here and there, for they will testify for him on the Day of Judgment.'

key_terms.يُفَرِّقُهَا: To distribute them (prayers in different places)

ai.seo_question: Where should optional (nafl) prayers be performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that optional (nafl) prayers should be distributed across various locations rather than performed in one place, emphasizing their spiritual weight. The Imam explains that each distinct location where a nafl prayer is offered serves as a witness for the individual on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the tangible spiritual merit of consistent, dispersed devotion. This view underscores the Shia emphasis on the cumulative value of voluntary acts of worship in securing divine intercession and reward.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Al-Hakam Bin Miskeen, from Abdullah Bin Ali Al-Sarrad who said,

‘Abu Kahmasy asked Abu Abdullahasws, so he said, ‘Should the man pray optional (Salāts) in one place or different?’ So heasws said: ‘No, but he should pray in different places, over her, and over these, for these (places) would be testifying for him on the Day of Judgment’.
en.sarwar: 18. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith it is narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from ’Abd Allah ibn Ali al-Sarrad who has said the following:

“Once, abu Kahmas asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Should a man perform his optional Salah (prayer) in one or in different places?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, one should perform them here and there because they testify in one’s favor on the Day of Judgment.’”
